newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australians hand in 250,000 banned weapons.
newsitem.headline: Australians hand in 250,000 banned weapons.

text.p: Australians have handed in more than 250,000 banned firearms under a buyback scheme launched after the Port Arthur massacre in April in which 35 people were killed by a lone gunman.

Attorney-General Daryl Williams said on Monday that 254,790 weapons, including military style self-loading rifles and pump-action shotguns, had been exchanged for almost A$120 million (US$95 million) since May.

Gun owners held mass protest rallies when laws barring almost all types of semi-automatic weapons were introduced, but opinion polls showed up to 90-percent support for a crackdown on firearms in the wake of the massacre.
Williams said the response to the programme had made Australia a world leader in firearms management.
Queensland state, which had previously failed to take part in the progamme, would begin compensating firearm owners and dealers this month, he said.

There are an estimated four million privately-owned firearms in Australia, a nation of 18 million, but the number of banned weapons has been difficult to gauge as most states did not have a register of guns.
Martin Bryant was sentenced to life imprisonment in November after the slaughter at the historic Port Arthur penal colony in the island state of Tasmania.
The Tasmanian Supreme Court was told he had bought several high-powered semi-automatic rifles in the months leading up to the massacre, despite not having a firearms licence.
